messages:
anna: Quick RFC follow-up on small-alloc fastpath vs compact-reorg tradeoffs. TL;DR: keep a very cheap fastpath for <=4KB allocations and avoid any compaction/locks on that path. Trigger an async, incremental compactor when per-tenant free-runway < 8MB or fragmentation_score > 0.6. Looking for concrete invariants, API boundaries, and failure modes.

javier: +1 to preserving the fastpath. question: how do we define fragmentation_score in a way that isn’t reactive/chaotic? we need something stable across bursts.

mike: initial formula idea: fragmentation_score = 1 - (largest_contiguous_free_runway / total_free_memory). sample on alloc hotspots and expose p50/p99. also track compaction_ms_per_mb so we can budget.

sophia: imo compaction must be incremental and budgeted. use reservation tokens so compactor never steals inference threads/saturates IO. config knobs: compaction_budget_ms_per_sec and compaction_bandwidth_mb_s. no stop-the-world.

anna: API boundary question: do we expose a sync maintenance API for compaction or only async hints from the runtime? i want to avoid sync ops on hot paths.

javier: ops will want a sync `compact_now` for maintenance windows. propose both: lightweight `compact_hint(range)` for hints, and `compact_now(range, force=false)` accessible to admins.

mike: if we add `compact_now`, it must be tenant-scoped and return a ticket/handle for polling rather than blocking RPCs. otherwise we risk huge latencies.

sophia: add allocator ABI extensions: `reserve_compaction_slots(n)` for the compactor to claim slowpath slots and `report_free_runway()` for the sampling layer. also pre/post hooks for KV cache eviction to avoid double-copy during compaction.

anna: perf safety: compaction copies can thrash NVMe. compactor should observe IO queue depth and backoff; use staged write buffer and rate-limit. Also prefer migrating cold pages first.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary compactor v1 pushed to rc cluster at 6880012360 :rocket:

javier: action items I'm hearing: - add metrics (frag_score, largest_runway, compaction_ms_per_mb) - prototype reservation API + allocator hooks - implement `compact_hint` + admin `compact_now` - canary compactor with default 1MB/s cap - draft RFC with failure modes and runbook.

mike: I'll take metrics + IO rate limiter + perf tests.

javier: I'll prototype reservation API + `compact_hint` semantics and the ticketing for `compact_now`.

anna: I'll write the RFC draft and own the runbook/fallback sections. RFC WIP: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/compact-reorg-draft (please comment). Sync scheduled tomorrow 11:00am PT. :calendar:

sophia: +1. also add a failure-mode: if compaction stalls or IO is saturated we should mark tenant "degraded" and route to fallback (evict to NVMe + reduce tenant concurrency).

anna: other follow-ups: 1) add unit & integration tests that assert no p99 regressions under heavy small-alloc workloads; 2) include telemetry for compaction CPU + IO cost per MB; 3) validate compactor on 90/10 read/write traffic pattern.

mike: noted, will add perf harness.

anna: thanks all — sounds like consensus on keeping fastpath, exposing hint + admin compact, and doing an incremental budgeted compactor with reservation tokens. will file PRs and link them to the RFC.

ops-bot: ci-bot: test pipeline started for canary at 6880012400 :white_check_mark:

javier: rough ETA: prototype by EOW, canary next week. anna will shepherd the RFC.

anna: great. tagging owners: @mike for metrics & rate-limiter, @javier for reservation/hint, @sophia for failure modes. meeting note saved.

mike: +1.

(End of thread)
